titulo_de: Ich kann, ich will, ich muss

will.en: I want to; I want to;

muss.en: I have to; I have to

texto: **Können** (power, know-how), **wollen** (want), **müssen** (have to) and **dürfen** (have permission) are irregular in singular, and the forms of **ich** and **er** are equal, without termination.
Its characteristic: the other verb goes in infinitive **al final** of the phrase. **Ich kann Auto fahren** (I can drive; literally «I can drive.»). **Ich muss heute arbeiten** (I have to work today).

bloques.titulo: Knowledge and power: the same verb
texto: In German **können** serves both a skill (**Ich kann schwimmen**, I can swim) and a possibility or a favor (**Kannst du mir helfen?**, can you help me?).
Denial goes before the infinitive: **Ich kann nicht schwimmen**.
**dürfen**: **Darf ich das Fenster öffnen?** is used to order permission (can I open the window?).

frases.en: You know how to drive, Sophie?

frases.de: Ja, ich kann Auto fahren. Aber ich kann nicht Fahrrad fahren!
frases.es: Sí, sé conducir. ¡Pero no sé montar en bici!
frases.en: Yeah, I know how to drive. But I can't ride a bike!

frases.de: Wirklich? Ich kann Fahrrad fahren, aber ich kann nicht schwimmen.
frases.es: ¿De verdad? Yo sé montar en bici, pero no sé nadar.
frases.en: Really? I can ride a bike, but I can't swim.

frases.de: Ich schwimme sehr gut. Und ich kann kochen.
frases.es: Yo nado muy bien. Y sé cocinar.
frases.en: I swim very well. And I can cook.

frases.de: Kannst du mir in der Küche helfen?
frases.en: Can you help me in the kitchen?
Sure. What do you want to eat?

frases.de: Ich möchte Nudeln. Aber zuerst muss ich einkaufen.
frases.es: Querría pasta. Pero antes tengo que hacer la compra.
frases.en: I'd like some money. But first I have to make the purchase.
analisis: I have to buy (with modal, the separable verb goes by and at the end)

bloques.pregunta: In a prayer with a modal verb, where is the main verb placed in infinitive?

opciones.texto: At the absolute end of the prayer.
opciones.explicacion: The conjugated modal verb goes in position 2 and the infinitive closes the prayer: «Ich kann gut schwimmen».
That's the Spanish romance structure, not the German order.

opciones.texto: In the first position before the subject.
opciones.explicacion: In the first position goes the subject or a complement.

bloques.pregunta: How is the acquired «I can swim.» skill expressed in German?

opciones.explicacion: The Modal «können» expresses both the ability and the practical skill learned.
The verb «wissen» expresses the knowledge of a theoretical fact or fact.
The modal verbs are never built with the «zu» particle.

bloques.pregunta: How does «I have to work today.» translate?

opciones.explicacion: The modal «müssen» expresses necessary obligation, with infinitive at the end.
«Haben» is not used to express obligation in German.
German manners do not support «zu» in the face of infinitive.
«Kann nicht» denies the possibility of performing the action expressed by the infinitive.
It would be «Ich will nicht kommen».

opciones.texto: I have no obligation to come.
opciones.explicacion: It would be «Ich muss nicht kommen».
The first plural form of the modal verb: «wir müssen».
It is the form for the 1st or 3rd person singular (ich / er).
It is the form for the 2nd person singular (du).
After the multima «kannst», the verb that complements goes at the end in infinitive.
A conjugated form in the present, incompatible with an auxiliary modal.
Substantive or informal peremptory form, not an infinitive.

bloques.frase: Mein Bruder kann sehr gut tanzen.

opciones.texto: My brother can dance very well.
opciones.explicacion: «Können» here expresses artistic skill with the infinite «tanzen».

opciones.texto: My brother can sing very well.
opciones.explicacion: Singing would be expressed with «singen».

opciones.texto: My brother can't dance in public.
opciones.explicacion: The original sentence is affirmative («sehr gut»).

bloques.explicacion: Subject + kann + nicht + object + infinitive at the end.
